statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES (orange). NQ lost the 29,308.50 floor that had held for two hours, extended to a 29,231.00 session low and now trades 29,290.25, down 159.25 points or 0.54%. ES confirmed the break at 7,645.25. That failed retracement followed by extension arrives alongside a 5.03% US 10-year, WTI up 2.13% on a Saudi pipeline outage and VIX at its session high of 18.03, so Tail crosses from 21 to 25 and Stress rises to 76.
recommendation: Tail at 25 maps to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The change from WATCH records a specific deterioration rather than a general worsening of tone. The 29,308.50 floor that survived roughly two hours of testing gave way, NQ extended 77.5 points below it to 29,231.00, and ES confirmed with its own new low at 7,645.25 instead of diverging as it did an hour ago. That is the failed-retracement-then-extension sequence the elevated band is meant to capture, and it no longer stands alone: the US 10-year is at 5.03%, its highest since 2007, the 2-year at 4.68% leaves the curve steepening from the long end, WTI trades at 103.55 up 2.13% within a 101.83 to 103.96 range, and cash VIX at 18.03 is up 5.44% and sitting at its session high rather than fading. Independent of the equity tape, the Saudi East-West pipeline remains shut after drone attacks traced to Iraq, removing a route that carried roughly four to five percent of global oil supply and bypassed an already disrupted Strait of Hormuz, with Yanbu export stocks reported at five to seven days. That is a genuine supply discontinuity rather than a scheduled event. Three observations hold the score at the lower edge of the elevated band instead of higher. NQ has retraced 59.25 points off its low, so mean reversion is visibly still functioning; the full overnight range of 264.25 points is 0.90 percent, which is orderly rather than violent; and index internals remain rotational, with Communication Services up 2.68 percent against Technology down 2.05 percent and megacaps split four up and four down. The declared danger window is 13:00 to 15:00 UTC around the US cash open, the first deeply liquid test of a structure that is now broken rather than merely tested. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection are unaffected by the mapped state.
headline: NQ breaks its defended 29,308.50 floor to a 29,231.00 low with ES confirming - Tail crosses to 25 as a 5.03% 10-year, a Saudi pipeline outage and a session-high VIX align
body:
The development of this hour is the one the previous assessment named as its invalidation. The 29,308.50 low that had held for roughly two hours broke, NQ extended to 29,231.00, and it now trades 29,290.25, down 159.25 points or 0.54% against a 29,449.50 prior close. The overnight range has widened from 186.75 points to 264.25 points, or 0.90%. Critically, ES confirmed this time: it printed 7,645.25 against the 7,660.25 marginal low that NQ declined to confirm an hour ago, and trades 7,653.25, down 0.51%. The prior hour's principal restraint, a divergence between the two index futures, has been removed.

The cross-asset picture has also tightened from conflicting to aligned. The US 10-year Treasury yield is at 5.03%, up about 4.5 basis points and the highest since 2007, with a separate reading of 5.041% recorded in the early US morning. The 2-year at 4.68% is up less than a basis point, so the repricing is long-end led and the curve is bear steepening, which is the configuration most directly punitive to long-duration technology valuations. Cash VIX at 18.03 is up 0.93 points or 5.44% and is trading at its session high, having ranged 17.40 to 18.03. An hour ago volatility was explicitly not corroborating; it now is.

The energy leg is a genuine supply discontinuity rather than a scheduled catalyst. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline remains shut after drone strikes on 13 September that hit two locations near Riyadh and Medina, with the launches traced to Maysan province in Iraq. The 1,200-kilometre line carries roughly four to five million barrels per day against a seven million barrel maximum, and it exists precisely to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, where flows are already reduced from over 20 million barrels per day to an estimated six to nine million amid the US-Iran conflict. Reported repair estimates range from days to five or six weeks, and Yanbu holds roughly five to seven days of export stocks. WTI trades at 103.55, up 2.13%, with Brent reported above 106 and one account putting it near 109. This is the kind of unresolved second information wave the framework treats as a Tail amplifier rather than a Stress input alone.

The equity-specific driver is unchanged and remains rotational. Monday's selloff followed industry calls to slow frontier AI model development, with the PHLX chip index falling 5.9% and trimming its 2026 gain to 57%. Latest-session moves show ARM down 9.74%, INTC down 5.59%, MU down 5.25%, AVGO down 4.77% and AMD down 4.40%, with all seven tracked semiconductor names negative. Against that, Communication Services gained 2.68% with GOOGL up 3.22% and META up 2.71%, and megacaps split four positive and four negative. Reporting characterises Monday's move as sentiment-driven, noting that no hyperscaler cut capital-expenditure guidance.

The restraints on the score are real and are the reason this is 25 rather than higher. NQ has already retraced 59.25 points off its low, so the mechanism the strategy depends on is visibly functioning. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Monday at 29,127.16, down 0.82%, but only after dipping to 28,867.67 and recovering more than 259 points into the close, which is a mean-reversion outcome. And a 0.90% overnight range is not a violent repricing. What has changed is that the count of independent current amplifiers has crossed from one or two to several, and one clean failed-retracement-and-extension cycle is now on the tape.

The two-day Federal Reserve meeting opened today, with the decision due at 18:00 UTC on Wednesday, beyond this forecast horizon. Market pricing for that decision shifted materially toward a rate increase after the Jackson Hole address, which is an unusual configuration against a long end already at multi-decade highs. Today's scheduled items are weekly ADP employment at 12:15 UTC, the NY Empire State manufacturing index at 12:30 UTC and a 20-year bond auction at 17:00 UTC; none had printed at the assessment cutoff.

The dominant mode is trend-down for the observed hour. The forecast holds 25 through the European mid-morning window that produced Monday's chip-led leg, eases to 24 and 23 into the pre-US lull, returns to 24 for the release window, and peaks at 27 across the declared 13:00 to 15:00 UTC danger window covering the cash open and the first full cash hour. That peak is deliberately kept well inside the elevated band because no opening structure has been observed and Monday's equivalent session recovered. Conditional risk then decays through the US afternoon, with a 25 tick for the 20-year auction, and falls to a cycle low of 18 in the Asian mid-session before rebuilding into the European open on Federal Reserve decision day.

lookbackSummary: The published record covers all 24 preceding clock hours. Tail ran 20 to 26 through Monday's European and US morning, peaking at 26 twice around the chip-led decline and the US cash open, then decayed through the US afternoon to 15 and to a 14 trough in the Asian session as price discovery turned orderly. It re-accelerated to 24 at 05:00 UTC when NQ first broke the 29,426.75 shelf with both index futures at extremes, eased to 20 and 21 through the European pre-open as a 76-point retracement resolved that structure, and has now crossed into the elevated band as the subsequent floor also failed. Stress held a 65 to 79 band throughout, reflecting a rate and energy backdrop that never reset. Confidence stayed between 86 and 89 on continuously available price-path evidence.
outlookSummary: The conditional path holds 25 for the remainder of this hour and across the 09:00 UTC window that produced Monday's chip-led leg, which now opens with the overnight floor already broken rather than intact. It eases to 24 for the European late morning and 23 for the pre-US lull, returns to 24 for the 12:15 and 12:30 UTC releases, and peaks at 27 across the declared 13:00 to 15:00 UTC danger window covering the US cash open and the first full cash hour. That peak stays at the lower half of the elevated band rather than higher because no opening structure has been observed and Monday's cash session recovered more than 259 points from its low. It steps down to 25 and 24 through the US afternoon, ticks back to 25 for the 17:00 UTC 20-year bond auction given the long-end repricing, and holds 24 into the closing hour. After the 20:00 UTC cash close conditional risk decays through 22, 21, 20 and 19 into the Asian session, bottoming at 18, before rebuilding through 19, 20, 21, 22 and 23 into the European open on Federal Reserve decision day. Stress tracks the same shape between 78 and 70 without leaving the high band, because a 5.03% 10-year and an unresolved Saudi pipeline outage do not reset overnight.
